correctness.rationale: For independent endpoints the side-choice factor is exact. Affine barycentric reduction and a monotonicity-in-interpolation calculation characterize every hit by explicit inequalities, whose two exact elementary integrals evaluate to F(r). Endpoint probabilities, atom at scale one, asymptotics and sharp side-length optimization follow. A separate Euclidean clipping program checked 975000 sampled chords across three triangles, and a second direct barycentric simulation checked six scales. Computations are only supporting tests, not proofs.

value.rationale: The exact full distribution of minimal intercepted centroidal-core scale is a natural geometric-probability invariant of random boundary chords. The conditional logarithmic law is shape-independent for all triangles and arbitrary side-selection weights; its nontrivial endpoint atom, sharp equilateral extremum, unattained flattening infimum, and universal small-scale coefficient fully classify how this statistic depends on triangle side lengths. It also produces an explicit negative shape-reconstruction result: only the sum of squared normalized side lengths remains visible in the whole law.
